To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The freezing of food is a complex, multi-stage process.
the accuracy of MW s and M b values is critical to the accuracy of predicted unfrozen water values.

(a) a new equation was developed for the prediction of the non-frozen water fraction during freezing of foods, (b) the parameters of this equation were derived from the published data on the non-frozen fraction and (c) the precision of the parameters was dependent upon the accuracy of the initial freezing point and (d) the precision of input variables (temperature, MW, M b, moisture content) and other physical parameters (density, heat capacity, thermal conductivity) were investigated to predict density
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing methods to predict the thermal properties of frozen foods.
the development of mathematical models that can predict the freezing characteristics of foods.
the development of mathematical models to predict thermal properties and the accuracy of these models for frozen food.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the precision of the thermal property values obtained from freezing curves of foods is dependent upon a number of factors.
the accuracy of the thermal properties of frozen foods depends on a number of factors.

the precision of thermal property data is influenced by the following factors in the order listed: (i) accuracy of measurement of the thermal property; (ii) precision of the thermal property data; (iii) precision of the temperature data; (iv) precision of the moisture content data; (v) precision of the initial freezing point temperature data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the freezing process is very complex and the accuracy of the prediction is very much dependent upon the accuracy of the input data.

the precision of the thermal property data for the frozen product depends on the precision of the initial freezing point, the mass fraction of the unfrozen water and on the mass fraction of dry matter.

the accuracy of the predicted values of the thermal properties of foods during freezing depends upon the accuracy of the input parameters, the accuracy of the equations and the accuracy of the experimental data used for the determination of the input parameters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of the proposed equation for predicting non-frozen water fraction during food freezing is very promising.
the precision of thermal property predictions depends on the precision of input parameters and on the thermal properties of the nonfrozen food.
the precision of thermal property data is highly dependent on the precision of the initial ice fraction.
